title: How Is Your Faith?
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Five questions to diagnose your faith. Faith is strong not because of us, but when it rests in Jesus and what he has done.
exhortation: My question this morning is: how is your faith? Here are a few questions to diagnose it.

One: is there a sin you've committed that can undo what Jesus has done? Two: is there shame in your past, carried around like a prosecuting attorney in your head, that can speak a word against the mercy of Jesus? Three: is there a sinister plan of the enemy or a scheme of the wicked that can unfinish what Jesus has finished? Four: is there a moment of anger, lust or pride that can reverse the decision of Jesus? Five: is there a pattern of foolishness or weakness that can erode the grace we have in Jesus? If your answer to every one of these is no, your faith is strong.

Ephesians 2:8-9 says, "For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast." We don't manufacture or earn our faith. It is a gift from God.

And in Galatians 3 Paul explains how it works: "For all who rely on works of the law are under a curse... Now it is evident that no one is justified before God by the law, for 'The righteous shall live by faith.'... Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us." We can't save ourselves. We can't obey the law perfectly. We all deserve the curse of death for our sins. But those who look in faith to Jesus and his perfect work will live. What makes our faith strong is not us. Our faith is strong when it rests in Jesus and what he has done.
prayer: Lord, we give you all the thanks. Build our faith as we rehearse the wonderful gospel of your grace and answer those questions.
There is no sin that can be held against us. There is no accuser you cannot answer. There is no failure you haven't already seen. Your blood covers all. In Christ alone we trust. Amen.
